description: Entity-to-repo mapping for the interactive metamodel viewer, generated from the OpenDEAM root model (dea-architecture-framework). Do not edit manually — regenerate with .github/scripts/generate_entity_graph.py. As of OpenDEAM v0.2.0 (ADR-0002), measurement is an orthogonal dimension: dimension entities carry `dimension` instead of `layer`, and relationships carry rel_type + cardinality (style is derived).

dimensions.name: Measurement Dimension
dimensions.kind: cross-cutting evaluative overlay (not a layer as of v0.2.0)

dimensions.name: AI & Automation Governance
dimensions.kind: cross-cutting policy overlay (not a layer, not "Responsible AI" as a separate structure)

dimensions.name: Semantic Dimension
dimensions.kind: cross-cutting concept graph (not a layer, not a static glossary)

entities.description: Terms governing cooperation with an ecosystem actor — cooperative or mandated.
entities.migration_note: Reallocated from L2-agreements to L1-agreements in v0.2.0 (ADR-0002 D2).

entities.description: External party that actively exchanges value with the enterprise — supplier, customer, regulator, partner.
A standing multi-sided structure the enterprise hosts for repeated exchange among many ecosystem actors (marketplace, partner API program, developer portal).
A point of interaction on a customer or user journey, across a specific channel.
An external or affected party whose relationship with the enterprise is engaged in or affected by enterprise processes.
A flow of value between the enterprise and an ecosystem actor — information, goods, or funds; inbound or outbound.
A reusable architecture pattern (e.g. API Gateway, Event Sourcing, CQRS) that resolves a recurring design problem.
A composed, reusable target-state design assembled from Architecture Patterns, providing a template for solution design.
entities.migration_note: Renamed from Reference Model (RM) in v0.4.0 (ADR-0004 D5) — now explicitly composed of Architecture Patterns rather than standing alone.

entities.description: A mechanism (process, technical, or organizational) that mitigates a Risk or enforces a Regulation.
A bounded, time-boxed test of a Signal's relevance to the enterprise before committing investment.

An enforceable constraint on technology or solution choices. Carries an enforcement maturity level (advisory | automated-warn | automated-block | platform-enforced) — modeling policy-as-code / platform-guardrail practice rather than a static compliance document someone checks against manually.
entities.migration_note: Renamed from Standard (STD) in v0.4.0 (ADR-0004 D4) — now governs Technology/Solution Component and implements Control, closing the gap where Technology claimed to be "governed via Standards" with no such relationship existing.

entities.description: A funded programme of work that realises one or more strategic objectives.
An externally imposed obligation (law, industry standard with force, contractual mandate) the enterprise must comply with.
A condition or event that threatens the enterprise's ability to persist or to realize a capability/objective.
A weak or early indicator of environmental change (market, technology, regulatory, competitive) worth tracking before it forces adaptation.
A high-level enterprise outcome the organisation seeks to achieve.
A non-binding, human-authored belief that guides decisions (e.g. API-first, prefer managed services). Informs one or more Guardrails; enforces nothing on its own.
entities.migration_note: Renamed from Principle (PR) in v0.4.0 (ADR-0004 D3) — a non-binding belief that informs Guardrails, rather than a standalone documentation-catalog entry.

entities.description: An emerging technology or technique being tracked (assess/trial/adopt/hold) prior to becoming a governed L5 Technology.
A performer of enterprise processes — human, team, system, or AI agent.
A grouping of business capabilities by organisational function; owned by an organizational unit.
A real-world entity of interest to the business (e.g. Customer, Order). The atom of the ECF matrix.
A structured set of activities that produces a defined outcome.
A service exposed to the business or to external consumers. Composite of capabilities, realised by solution components.
An ability the business possesses or requires to deliver value. Maps to ECF coordinates.
A deliberate effort to shift Skills, Roles, or culture within an Organizational Unit, typically funded by an Investment Initiative.
Liquid or near-liquid economic value the enterprise holds (accounts, instruments, funding lines). Catalog instances include cash, credit facilities, and similar.
Legally protected non-physical economic value (patents, trademarks, brand equity, licenses). Catalog instances include a specific trademark registration or license.
A unit of organisation that owns capabilities, runs processes, and is custodian for business objects.
Tangible assets requiring an ongoing maintenance regime (equipment, vehicles, premises, inventory stock). Catalog instances include an oven, a van, a warehouse shelf.
The economic/physical substrate a bounded entity maintains to persist, distinct from what it exchanges (L1) or builds digitally (L4/L5).
entities.completeness_contract: Any T2 catalog specializing Resource must classify instances along exactly one of three dimensions: liquidity (-> Financial Resource), maintenance regime (-> Physical Resource), or legal protection type (-> Intangible Resource). Each dimension implies a distinct governance/relationship pattern, not merely a different label. (ADR-0005 D3)

entities.description: A defined set of required Skills and responsibilities that an Actor fulfills within an Organizational Unit.

Abstract parent of ApplicationComponent, InfrastructureComponent, IntegrationComponent (discriminated union by component_type). Concrete subclasses are allocated to L5; see specializes on APC/IFC/IGC below. (ADR-0002 D3)
A capability an individual Actor possesses or must develop. Distinct from Business Capability, which belongs to the enterprise, not a person.
An end-to-end collection of value-creating activities spanning multiple capabilities and processes.
A machine-learning or AI model that augments or replaces human decision-making within a capability. May declare governed_by (RSK/CTL/REG ids) per the ai-automation-governance dimension.
A persistent data structure (table, document, graph node) that realises one or more business objects.
A digital representation (twin) of a stakeholder or actor for authentication, authorisation, and traceability.
A curated, discoverable, governed dataset or data service with clear ownership and SLAs (data-mesh pattern).
A significant state change or business occurrence that business objects participate in.
Data given context and form for a specific consuming purpose (a report, dashboard, invoice) — distinct from the raw Data Entity it's contextualized from.
A classification of information by sensitivity and regulatory regime (PII, PHI, PCI).
Applied know-how made explicit and durable, existing independent of any one Actor — distinct from Skill (L3), which an Actor personally possesses.
A running instance of an AI/ML Model, hosted on an Application Component, with its own version, monitoring state, and health.
Drift, performance-degradation, or outcome-quality feedback captured from Events, used to trigger retraining of an AI/ML Model.
A deployable unit of an application system. SubClass of SolutionComponent with component_type='application'.
A contract defining the request/response shape of a service interface.
An IaC-managed resource that hosts solution components. SubClass of SolutionComponent with component_type='infrastructure'.
A component that bridges systems via APIs, queues, file transfers. SubClass of SolutionComponent with component_type='integration'.
A shared infrastructure or runtime service consumed by multiple application components.
A functional capability exposed by a single application or system.
A technology choice (language, framework, runtime, database) governed via Guardrails, motivated by Tenets.

A canonical, definable unit of meaning (business term or classification node) that other entities link to via defined_by. Merged from Glossary Term + Taxonomy Node in v0.4.0 (ADR-0004 D2); framed as a queryable concept graph, not a static glossary document. No longer allocated to a layer/building_block — belongs to orthogonal_allocators.semantic-dimension.

A measured quantity used to evaluate outcomes against targets. MECE taxonomy: kpi | health | maturity | performance | adoption | compliance | risk. No longer allocated to a layer/building_block as of v0.2.0 — belongs to orthogonal_allocators.measurement-dimension instead (ADR-0002 D1).

relationship_definitions.name: Composes
relationship_definitions.definition: The target is structurally part of the source and normally has a dependent lifecycle (composition, section 14).

relationship_definitions.name: Aggregates
relationship_definitions.definition: The target participates in the source but retains an independent lifecycle (aggregation, section 14).

relationship_definitions.name: Specializes
relationship_definitions.definition: The source is a more specific form of the target (generalization/specialization hierarchy).

relationship_definitions.name: Instantiates
relationship_definitions.definition: A concrete instance is created from a type or model (section 5).

relationship_definitions.name: Realizes
relationship_definitions.definition: The source architectural element provides the realization of an abstract capability, service, or outcome (section 5).

relationship_definitions.name: Implements
relationship_definitions.definition: An implementation satisfies a specification, requirement, or design (section 5). Narrowed: not used for capability realization (use realizes) or technology enablement (use supports).

relationship_definitions.name: Operationalizes
relationship_definitions.definition: A policy, tenet, or strategy is translated into operational practice (section 5).

relationship_definitions.name: Depends On
relationship_definitions.definition: The source requires the target for some purpose, without containment or realization semantics (section 14).

relationship_definitions.name: Requires
relationship_definitions.definition: The source cannot fulfil its definition without the target (mandatory dependency).

relationship_definitions.name: Enables
relationship_definitions.definition: The source makes the target possible or materially more effective, without being required by it.

relationship_definitions.name: Constrains
relationship_definitions.definition: The source limits the permissible design or behaviour space of the target.

relationship_definitions.name: Flows To
relationship_definitions.definition: Information, material, control, or value moves from the source to the target.

relationship_definitions.name: Produces
relationship_definitions.definition: The source creates or emits the target as an output.

relationship_definitions.name: Consumes
relationship_definitions.definition: The source takes the target as an input it uses up or processes.

relationship_definitions.name: Exchanges
relationship_definitions.definition: The source and target participate in a bidirectional exchange of value, data, or signals.

relationship_definitions.name: Serves
relationship_definitions.definition: The source delivers value or service to the target party or channel.

relationship_definitions.name: Provides
relationship_definitions.definition: The source makes the target service or capability available to consumers.

relationship_definitions.name: Uses
relationship_definitions.definition: The source consumes the target service or resource as offered (usage, not depletion — contrast consumes).

relationship_definitions.name: Exposes
relationship_definitions.definition: The source presents the target as an accessible interface, product, or representation to consumers.

relationship_definitions.name: Performs
relationship_definitions.definition: The source actor or organizational unit carries out the target process or function (section 12).

relationship_definitions.name: Executes
relationship_definitions.definition: The source system function or component carries out the target process or activity automatically.

relationship_definitions.name: Orchestrates
relationship_definitions.definition: The source coordinates the execution ordering and interaction of the targets.

relationship_definitions.name: Triggers
relationship_definitions.definition: The source event or signal initiates the target process, experiment, or retraining.

relationship_definitions.name: Governs
relationship_definitions.definition: The source directs, constrains, or oversees the target through policy, agreement, or strategy.

relationship_definitions.name: Mandates
relationship_definitions.definition: The source imposes a binding obligation on the target (regulatory or policy force).

relationship_definitions.name: Controls
relationship_definitions.definition: The source mitigates, protects against, or otherwise controls the target risk or exposure.

relationship_definitions.name: Owns
relationship_definitions.definition: The source holds ownership of the target — accountability for its lifecycle and value.

relationship_definitions.name: Accountable For
relationship_definitions.definition: The source holds single-point accountability for the target (RACI 'A').

relationship_definitions.name: Responsible For
relationship_definitions.definition: The source performs or manages the target day-to-day (RACI 'R'), including custodianship and role fulfilment.

relationship_definitions.name: Threatens
relationship_definitions.definition: The source risk exposes the target to potential harm or failure (risk relation, section 17 placement per D5).

relationship_definitions.name: Represents
relationship_definitions.definition: One information representation corresponds to another conceptual entity (section 5).

relationship_definitions.name: Informs
relationship_definitions.definition: The source provides knowledge, evidence, or meaning that shapes the target (incl. semantic definition and weak influence — section 17).

relationship_definitions.name: Curates
relationship_definitions.definition: The source selects, organizes, and maintains the target as governed content or product.

relationship_definitions.name: Publishes
relationship_definitions.definition: The source makes the target event or information available to subscribers.

relationship_definitions.name: Subscribes To
relationship_definitions.definition: The source consumes publications of the target event or information feed.

relationship_definitions.name: Trained On
relationship_definitions.definition: The source AI/ML model is trained on the target data product or dataset.

relationship_definitions.name: Derived From
relationship_definitions.definition: The source is derived from the target information, event, or actor knowledge (lineage).

relationship_definitions.name: Assessed By
relationship_definitions.definition: The source is evaluated by the target assessment instrument, experiment, or framework.

relationship_definitions.name: Measured By
relationship_definitions.definition: The source's performance, health, or maturity is quantified by the target metric.

relationship_definitions.name: Evidenced By
relationship_definitions.definition: The source relationship or claim is supported by the target evidence artefact (section 6).

relationship_definitions.name: Benchmarked Against
relationship_definitions.definition: The source is compared against the target reference, standard, or peer.

relationship_definitions.name: Transitions To
relationship_definitions.definition: The source evolves into the target state, maturity, or technology over time (CR-6 will add temporal semantics).

relationship_definitions.name: Replaces
relationship_definitions.definition: The source takes over the function of the target, which is retired.

relationship_definitions.name: Supersedes
relationship_definitions.definition: The source version or concept supersedes the target in definition or governance.

relationship_definitions.name: Migrates To
relationship_definitions.definition: The source is moved to the target platform, component, or state during a change initiative.

relationship_definitions.name: Maps To
relationship_definitions.definition: An explicit crosswalk or correspondence between two modelling systems or classification schemes (section 9). NOT a generic 'somehow related'.

relationship_definitions.name: Traces To
relationship_definitions.definition: Audit lineage from the source to the target artefact that justifies or originates it.

relationship_definitions.name: Supports
relationship_definitions.definition: The source contributes to the target's function, funding, or effectiveness without realizing, enabling, or being required by it.
